## MP-06f Review — auxiliary-authority.sql

**Migration** (`supabase/migrations/20260101001700_auxiliary_authority.sql`): revokes `REFERENCES` on exactly the 19 enumerated tables (lines 3–7, count verified) and `ALL` on `sequence public.audit_log_id_seq` (line 10), both from `public, anon, authenticated` only — matches the plan's "REFERENCES 19 table targets plus ALL on audit_log_id_seq" scope. No grants added, no old migrations touched.

**Composite PK handling** — `auxiliary-authority.sql` lines 9–12 derive `k`/`typ` generically from `pg_index`/`pg_attribute` per table, so `rate_limits` (composite PK `(key, window_start)`, confirmed at `20260101000300_rate_limits.sql:18`) gets a real two-column FK probe (`add foreign key(key,window_start) references public.rate_limits(key,window_start)`), not a single-column stand-in. Correct.

**Sequence denial/restoration** — lines 23–35 separately probe `read` (SELECT), `setval` (UPDATE), `nextval` (USAGE), each caught on `insufficient_privilege` and recorded independently — matches "sequence SELECT/USAGE/UPDATE denied ... separately." Red-oracle restoration is done outside the SQL file, in `scripts/test-db-security.py:104–106`, which regrants one of `select|usage|update` to `anon` per case and expects the matching denial message (`read`/`nextval`/`setval` mapped correctly at line 106) — a real, isolated restoration per privilege, not a blanket grant.

**Trusted insert / default sequence** — `audit_log.id` is `bigserial` (`20260101000000_init.sql:250`), so `audit_log_id_seq` is genuinely owned by the column; the service-role insert at `auxiliary-authority.sql:46–49` exercises the untouched default, and since the revoke targets only `public/anon/authenticated`, the table owner's default-sequence path is preserved by Postgres semantics, not overridden. Correct behavior, no bypass introduced.

**Nontransactional sequence restore-in-finally** — confirmed in `test-db-security.py:40–54`: `run_suite` snapshots `last_value/is_called` before every auxiliary call, restores via `setval` in a `finally` (so it runs even when the wrapped call raises `RuntimeError` from `h.psql`), and asserts equality after restore. Called 5× per reset (4 broken-signature loop iterations + 1 clean run at line 119) × 2 resets = 10, matching the expected count.

**Counts** — SUITES expected values sum to 289 (46 new + 243 prior) enforced at line 125; `regressions_detected == 42` (21 signatures/reset × 2, 4 of which are the new auxiliary red cases) and `sequence_restorations == 10` are both asserted at line 135. All figures match the packet's expected 46/243, 4/17, and 10/2-resets figures.

**No issues found.** No PUBLIC-only fallback, no billing fallback, no scope creep beyond the 19 tables + one sequence. Did not run SQL myself.
